requirements.rule: Every temporal stream declares a clock domain.
Every cross-clock mapping declares source clock, target clock, offset, drift model, and estimated error when a cross-clock conversion is used.
Every spatial value declares coordinate frame and units.
Every transform declares source-to-target direction and validity interval.
Persistent entities maintain identity across observations, representations, annotations, events, and simulator actors.
Every representation declares a role.
Every external asset declares URI, media type, digest, and license when license is known.
Every asset can be resolved deterministically and verified by digest.
Dataset-scale deployments declare a manifest with shard and index catalogs; opening or validating a dataset does not require recursive filesystem scans or object-store listings.
Every shard and materialized index declares URI, media type, digest, schema reference, partition keys, and row/object counts where available.
Persistent IDs are globally scoped by declared namespace when crossing dataset boundaries.
Dataset versions are append-only snapshots; deletion or replacement uses tombstones or supersession records.
Resolvers declare supported URI schemes, cache policy, and mirror priority for deterministic resolution at scale.
Every action channel declares control mode, parameterization, frame, and units.
Command time and effective-time semantics are declared.
Every world revision is immutable and content-addressed.
Every episode references one base world revision and an ordered delta sequence.
Every derived representation records source and transformation provenance.
Inferred or reconstructed values declare uncertainty and source status.
Every conversion emits a machine-readable loss report.
Dataset splits may enforce world, entity, source-capture, reconstruction-run, generated-asset-family, and site disjointness.
Replay records simulator, version, solver, timestep, materials, initialization assumptions, and tolerance envelope.
